title: How Face ID-style 3D face scanning actually works
description: Face unlock on phones like iPhones doesn't just compare photos. It builds a depth map with invisible infrared dots.

scenes.big: Face unlock reads depth, not a photo
scenes.say: Face unlock doesn't just take a picture of you. It builds a three-D map of your face.
Apple says Face ID needs depth data, which a flat photo doesn't contain. It also checks that your eyes are open and you're paying attention.

steps: Neural engine builds a math model
Secure Enclave compares it to yours
scenes.say: A projector casts more than thirty thousand invisible infrared dots on your face. A camera reads how the pattern bends. A neural network turns it into a mathematical model, and a secure chip compares it with the one you enrolled.
Apple quotes odds under one in a million for a random person. Twins and young children raise that. Five failed tries and it wants your passcode. The data stays on the device, encrypted.
So it's a depth scan, not a selfie. Follow for more hardware, explained.
